_doc: Acknowledged reds — vibe-ic#1025. Adjudicated by
vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/programs/gate_red_since_check.py.
A row here grants NO leniency. The hygiene suite still exits 1 for every
FAIL exactly as it did before this file existed, so there is nothing a row
can silence and no green a row can buy. The ONLY thing a row does is start
a clock that gate_red_since_check will fail on once `max_commits` is
exceeded. Adding a row is therefore taking on a deadline, never escaping
one.
Delete the row in the SAME commit that fixes the gate. A row that outlives
its truth is failed as `stale`, because a stale acknowledgement is
indistinguishable to the next reader from a live one, and it is the row
that gets believed.
FIELDS
gate         the gate's label EXACTLY as tools/ci/_gate_dispatch.sh
records it. A label that matches nothing in the record is
failed as `stale`, so a drifting label cannot go quiet.
since        the commit at which the gate went red. The clock is commits
and not wall time so that every reader of the same tree
computes the same age with no persisted run history.
max_commits  how many commits this red may survive before this file
fails the landing gate. Required — an acknowledgement with
no bound never comes due, which is the state being removed.
owner        the issue or PR that will close it.
why          why it is red, in one sentence, for the reader who finds
this file six weeks from now.
adjudicated  present when a ruling has been written down for this row: the
verdict and where to read it. A row carrying one is NOT to be
renewed by moving `since` forward -- the ruling replaced the
question the deadline was asking.
bound_because why max_commits is THAT number and not a larger one. Not read
by the adjudicator -- read by the reviewer, who is the only
defence against a bound chosen for comfort. A bound whose
reason is 'so the board stays green' is the thing this file
exists to catch.

acknowledged.why: floorplan_hints, power_budget_uw and sdc_constraints_path are read by a checker and populated in 0 of the 4 documents that carry them, so the consumer cannot tell empty from clean.
acknowledged.bound_because: The fix is in vibeic/benchmark-data, not in this repo: either the L-docs populate the three fields or the checker declares them optional, and a cross-repository change needs a round trip. 210 commits is three days at the measured rate. It is the longest bound here and it is still 290 short of the ceiling. || SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22, kept because it was true when measured: the corpus moved (b971220) and now holds NO L-doc carrying a `fields` object at all, so the fix described above — populate the three fields, or declare them optional — is no longer the question. The gate returns rc 2 UNDETERMINED over a zero denominator, which is correct behaviour; what is wrong is the DISPATCH recording rc 2 as FAIL. The bound is not what needs revisiting here.
acknowledged.adjudicated: REAL FINDING — stays red until fixed, NOT renewed. docs/research/2026-08-21-corpus-gate-adjudication.md

acknowledged.why: 113 baseline entries now resolve and must be shrunk out of the baseline before it becomes a standing waiver, and 4 documents cite proofs they do not ship.
acknowledged.bound_because: Two halves with different costs: shrinking the baseline is one --write-baseline run, and the 4 dangling citations need someone to decide whether the document or the missing file is wrong. 140 commits is two days at the measured rate, which is the decision half; the mechanical half could be done today. || FIGURES SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22: the corpus moved (b971220) and shrank from 1037 enumerated files to 70. It is now 66 contributing documents of 70, 28 citations, 132 baseline entries resolving and 5 dangling — not the 113 and 4 above. The SHAPE of the reasoning stands (a mechanical half and a decision half) and so does the bound; only the counts moved.
